Because I would then invite the parties to get a Google Earth picture of the situation, and then you would be able to explain to us more concretely what the situation was which you said you had knowledge of. Do you think you could do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it has to do with the old town, then that is part of Kotor Varos. It is an elevation above Kotor Varos and it's called Kotor. And approximately it is about 400 to 500 metres away from houses. I mean, houses are away from that fortress. Well, that can be obtained. So, yes, we can take a look at this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we were talking about 5.11, which was concentrated fire of the old town and -- from a firing position in the area of Jelsingrad. Is that Kotor Varos as far as you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Jelsingrad is an integral part of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you would have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a factory, otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So if you would have a map, you could indicate exactly on that map or on that aerial view where the old town is, where the fortress is, and you could indicate to us at -- you said the fortress is 4- to 500 metres from any houses, because we could then try to do that so we better understand your testimony and that we have more concrete basis to evaluate the evidence, both in this order and your testimony as a witness. Could the parties provides -- I take it that you would agree that it must be possible to get a Google Earth view or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We could get a current one. That would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- [Overlapping speakers] ... we could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, there always is the issue of whether the situation is the same. However, an old fortress usually doesn't move that much over the last 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I might inquire of the witness. I believe he indicated it does not exist anymore, but I may have misheard that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he then perhaps could tell us where it had been so that we -- let's -- let's give it a try to get matters concrete and understandable for this Chamber as well. We take a break and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? May I, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to give you my comment. Today that still exists. The concentrated fire there, that it was marked there, that doesn't mean that it was targeted in the first place. It doesn't mean that a single shell was fired at that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it does exist to this day. Nothing has changed. That edifice is still there. The only change can be in the number of houses there now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are just looking at this moment at the order, not whether fire finally opened or not but just what the order tells us, and to check the explanation you gave us, to see that rather than to just hear what you're telling us. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to come in. Have the parties been successful in getting some aerial views of Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that we gave the same thing you are holding in black and white.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of the problems is that there is no scale on it. If there would be any way to get a scale so that we know what is a kilometre and what is 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have images coming. They are not here yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And they are with a scale on it?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'll have that inquiry made right now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would suggest, Ms. Bibles, that you just continue until you have the material ready which you would like to use. Of course, if it would be available electronically, that would even be better. But we also can work still with a good old -- the -- I've forgotten even what the name is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The ELMO, yes. The ELMO, yes. The good old ELMO. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In your testimony this morning, you described at fair length a contact with a young Muslim girl. I'd like to ask you about your knowledge regarding some of the Muslim villages or non-Serb villages that the Trial Chamber has heard evidence about. Are you aware that the Kotor Vares Light Infantry Brigade committed killings in a village named Dobovici in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get the interpretation. I didn't receive any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll check whether there is any problem and whether you're on the right channel. Do you now hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you now, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Bibles. And perhaps you'll resume from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In your testimony this morning, you described at fair length your contact with a young Muslim girl. I'd like to ask about your knowledge about some of the non-Serb villages that the Trial Chamber has heard about in Kotor Varos. Are you aware that the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade committed killings in Dobovici in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of such information. As far as I know, the Kotor Varos Brigade did not commit that. As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has also heard evidence that in a Muslim village, Hrvacani, the village was attacked in June and that the elderly individuals who stayed behind were killed after the attack. This Trial Chamber has heard that in the village of Hanifici, which signed a loyalty oath, that there were massacres of unarmed men. The Trial Chamber has heard that in the village of Cirkino Brdo -- excuse me, C-i-r-k-i-n-o Brdo, which also signed a loyalty oath, that there were massacres of unarmed individuals. And I can just tell you that there were -- there has been other evidence in front of this Trial Chamber regarding the status of villages and civilians in Kotor Varos. Now, sir, wouldn't you agree that in August to December of 1992 when you testified or when you -- after you had joined the brigade, that there really were many villages in which Muslims and Croats would not feel comfortable returning to their homes?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for those villages and relations, and when we're talking about the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade, what I know is that that brigade definitely had no part in all of that. The reason why I'm saying that is because the Kotor Varos Brigade was not capable of doing anything like that due to its strength. In the initial period, the brigade was deployed exclusively in local communes. It was in defensive positions. Those people were from the neighbouring villages; for example, the Maslovar company was at an elevation between Garici and Maslovar. Those people didn't go anywhere from that place. For example, the Vagani company, which was in the Vagani village, was in defensive positions. Those forces were not moved. They didn't execute any assaults. I am not ruling out that some other formations did that, but I wasn't there in that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, and I'll just tell you the Prosecution position based on the evidence that's been in front of this Trial Chamber, is that in August of 1992 the Kotor Vares Light Infantry Brigade did attack Dobovici and did kill civilians. So I submit to you that your attempt to portray the light brigade and the events in Kotor Varos is somewhat different that the evidence that's been presented in front of this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you. Again, I'm repeating the fact that we didn't have a unit in the Dabovci village area or in Vrbanci generally, which is a larger settlement that would be capable of executing any action of that kind. That area was not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, are you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the area where our brigade was located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you telling us what your conclusions are, or are you telling you us that you have knowledge about them not being involved in any of these attacks just described? Because logic is not the same as facts. So you can tell us that this was the strength, but to say they were not strong enough to do this, that is a conclusion. You see the difference? So if you want to emphasize that the unit was too small or not, then tell us how strong it was. But whether that allows for certain conclusions, that's an entirely different matter. So could you clearly distinguish between the two - that is, facts. And, of course, especially if you say it may have been other units. If you have any knowledge about which units, then of course we'd like to know that as well. Please, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to turn to paragraphs 7 through 20 in your statement, the events in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but perhaps after I intervene, Ms. Bibles, it would be fair for the witness to have an opportunity to express himself. Do you know of any other facts, so I'm not seeking conclusions, but do you know any facts which are relevant for us to decide whether or not it could have been members of your brigade that were involved in matters during your absence as mentioned by Ms. Bibles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here I'm talking about my knowledge. That's one thing. My knowledge, that members of the Light Kotor Varos Brigade did not take part or did not commit any such thing in the Dabovac [as interpreted] area. This is my knowledge. That's one thing. The other thing is my conclusion that relates to the combat capacity of that unit, of the Kotor Varos Brigade, which was in the sector of Vrbanci. It was in a different part where it was deployed. That was where the forces of the 22nd Infantry Brigade were deployed. When we're talking about the Kotor Varos Brigade, my information is that this was not committed by members of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said your knowledge is that they did not take part, but you were not there at the time. What then is your knowledge based on if you weren't there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mostly it's based on conversations, stories by the unit commanders who simply did not take part in those activities; i.e., in what those units did. Our units which were part of the Kotor Varos Brigade were made up of people who were almost in civilian clothing, and in certain areas they were defending the area. They were on the lines defending their houses. They were at those positions. There were -- they were units of the Kotor Varos Brigade who were never moved from those positions. We didn't have an operational part that could do anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say conversations, stories where the unit commanders who simply did not take part in those activities. Did you discuss such events with them? Did you discuss what is described by Ms. Bibles as bad things done to civilian population? Did you discuss that with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not speak with them directly, but the story about that, when we're talking about these unfortunate ugly things that happened, no one mentioned any forces of the Kotor Varos Brigade. So that is that story that the Kotor Varos Brigade did not commit anything of that nature in that period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What in those stories were the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. There was some people there who committed that. Who they were, though, is something that I really have no information about. I really don't know anything about it. I said that there were forces of the 22nd Infantry Brigade in that area as well, close to that inhabited settlement that the -- that Madam -- the Prosecutor mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To simply summarise: You heard stories, you had conversations which did not point at members of your brigade being involved in it but also not clearly defining who then would have committed those acts. That is, in short, what you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with your assertion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you take the position in view of what you know about strength, et cetera, et cetera, that those stories sound credible to you, although you were unable to personally verify. Is that also well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with that. Yes, I can agree with what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And perhaps just one quick follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you would agree that the 22nd Infantry Brigade had the combat capacity to do the events that I have described?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is this: The 22nd Infantry Brigade was more operational than the Kotor Varos Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: To go back to the issue of the command structure in your brigade or above your brigade, you testified previously that a Lieutenant-Colonel Janko Trivic replaced Peulic as the commander for the operational group under which your brigade fell; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And this change in command occurred in very late October, beginning of November 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm when it arrived. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you know whether this change in the command structure related to Lieutenant-Colonel Peulic's failure to resolve the military issue at Vecici?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have absolutely no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Okay. Now turning to Grabovica, you would agree that the story and the events at Grabovica actually start with Vecici; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have P440 on our screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: This is the 30 October 1992 order for combat operations signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Novakovic. And, sir, I see the B/C/S version has come up on your screen. You would agree that this is the plan for a combat operation against Vecici; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with what you are asserting because that does not relate to the operation and the plan regarding Vecici. This refers to routing -- or, actually, breaking up the ring around the town of Kotor Varos and opening up a communication that was very important to us, the Kotor Varos-Vagan village road. That's one argument. Another argument was to resolve the question of --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in point 1, this order for carrying out combat operations begins with describing events through the media and in negotiations regarding the citizens of village of Vecici; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It begins with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And then when we go to the second paragraph under point 1, we see that: "According to the available data, the armed part (about 400-450 Ustasha-Muslim soldiers) is planning a successive withdrawal from the area of the village of Vecici ..." And a route is listed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now let's turn to the next page, and I'm looking for point 4.12, and I believe it's the second page in both versions. I see that we're expanding this to make it easier to read 4.12.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, we see that this is again an order to the 82 -millimetre Mortar Platoon, and it states under A: "In preparation for operations: "- open fire on the agreed signal on the villages of Vecici, Brizine, Bajrico Brdo, Velino Brdo, the village of Durici and trig point 648." So, sir, this is an order to fire on these villages; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's distorting the evidence. It says "the area of the villages ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The area. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, you should be precise in that, especially in view of the matter apparently in dispute. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Where were you located as part of this operation as described in this order?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I do not remember all these actions very well. I don't even know that we were the ones who were executing these actions. I don't remember us having any actions in relation to the village of Vecici. The only thing that we did do in relation to the village of Vecici was to sweep the terrain and not any combat actions or attacks. I don't remember our brigade ever actually carrying out this activity. I can see the document, I confirm the document, I confirm Novakovic's signature, but simply the way that I remember things now, I don't remember us carrying out that kind of action at all. We did have some actions in relation to the village of Vecici. This feature here, up to Bajrica Brdo, up to Bajrica Brdo, that was where we were mopping up. I know that. That is what we did do. As for this other thing, simply it's not something that I have at all in my recollection. I cannot remember anything of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's make this much more simple, then. Where were you when Lieutenant-Colonel Novakovic ordered you to go to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Lieutenant-Colonel Novakovic told me to go to Grabovica, first I toured some of the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Where --

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- were you?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- for the most part -- I was probably in the Kotor Varos sector, or in Kotor where the 2nd Infantry Company was deployed, or possibly in the sector of the 1st Infantry Company which was somewhere in the northern sector of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So is the answer that you don't remember where you were but you were somewhere in the field of operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the Kotor Varos area. That's where the units were deployed. But I cannot remember exactly where I was on this one allocation or the other location. I was touring the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: How did you get to Grabovica? Were you in a vehicle with other individuals? Were you with Lieutenant-Colonel Novakovic? Could you describe how you got to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I came to the Kotor Varos command, Commander Novakovic told me that he had some information that a Muslim column was supposed to arrive at Grabovica and that Muslim column was to be received. Then he told me, "Vojo, go up there to Grabovica and help up there so you can see" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, why not answer the question: How did you get there? Did you go by car, did you -- were you alone? That's the question. Could you please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will answer the question. I thought I would make this introduction so that it would be clearer to you, but it's all right. I went to Grabovica by car, a yellow Golf, and I had one person in my escort.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that the column had surrendered when you were sent to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any other information other than a column of Muslim inhabitants was supposed to arrive at Grabovica. That's all I knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get from the command post in Kotor Vares to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to say now. Perhaps half an hour. Let's say half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When you arrived at Grabovica, where specifically did you first go? Because you drove in.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drove up to the command of the Grabovac Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Can you describe for us, and this may have been covered in your testimony, and I apologise if it was, was it day or night-time when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came to Grabovica, it was already getting dark. It was dusk.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Who was the commanding officer at Grabovica when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Grabovica Company, Mile Kljajic was the one who was waiting for me when I got there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When you spoke with him, did he tell you that the column had surrendered?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't have any information about that other than the same information that I had, that a column of Muslims was due to arrive in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you have any information regarding where the column was located at the time you arrived?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: How long was it before you knew that the column or the people in the column had surrendered to the VRS forces?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for that time, I don't know. And this concept, "surrendered," and all of that, yes, the column appeared in Grabovica. And now as for how that came to be, how this contact occurred at positions between our army and those people, that is something I really don't know. I mean, the column appeared somewhere perhaps...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. So the first time that you saw the column, you were in Grabovica and people were being brought to Grabovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived in one column. It was a mixed column of men and women. They were in a column in pairs, two by two. And when the column arrived, our soldiers were with the column. They were escorting the column. I mean, soldiers of the Grabovac Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In paragraph 8 of your statement, you described that the column that arrived in Grabovica was taken to the football - or I think the English translation is "soccer" - field. Were you present when the column was taken to the football field?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present. The soccer field or the football field was right next to the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, you would agree at this point when you first saw these individuals that they were prisoners of the VRS; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I would use that term, "prisoners," because I don't know the mode or the status and all of that from the moment when there was contact between the Grabovac Company and the Muslims what the status was. I mean, it doesn't have to mean that they had been taken prisoner. Perhaps that column was being secured.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Maybe I'll make this easier, and I'm sort of reflecting a question that you received earlier from the Trial Chamber: These individuals were not free to leave, were they?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what I could say by way of an answer to that question. Well, they came there to Grabovica. I've already mentioned to His Honour that the situation then was such that any movement of theirs at that part would have threatened their lives a lot more than if they stayed there on that spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, sir, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put an additional question. Was this group of people escorted by others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This group of people was escorted by the soldiers from the Grabovac Company. They had taken them from the Duboka location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: By the time the column arrived in Grabovica, it was dark, wasn't it -- or correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In paragraph 8, you describe that Novakovic ordered you or directed you to put women and children on the ground floor in the school and then upstairs. When did Lieutenant-Colonel Novakovic arrive in Grabovica in relationship to your relationship in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not really put that right in the first part of your sentence or question. As for when Novakovic arrived in Grabovica, he arrived perhaps 15 or 20 minutes after I had arrived in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: After he arrived, he was the commander on scene; right? He was ...

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You've described that women and children, and the reason I went to that is women and children were to be placed on one floor, and I think you described in your statement the able-bodied men on the upper floor. Who directed that women and children be separated from the men?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Commander Novakovic that ordered that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did he actually do this or announce this to the group personally?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While they were at the sports field, that's what he said. That first the women and children were to be separated and taken to the school and he said that they would be staying in a classroom. According to his order, they were put up on the ground floor. At that moment I wasn't by him. I was at a different position where I was waiting for weapons to arrive.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's first follow the women and children. Once the women and children were separated from the able-bodied men, were they lined up before they were taken into the school?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice that. I was far away. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So you were not there when the women and children were addressed or spoken to?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was away -- no, no. No. He addressed the entire group at the sports field. So when he was addressing them, I was there next to him at that moment when he said that. He said, Please line up here, and now we're going to see. First the women and children would be separated and then they would slowly walk to the school, and over there you will be put up in a classroom. As he was saying that --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead, I'm sorry. Go ahead, I'm sorry. After he said that, the women and children actually got up and -- and left the area?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "got up"? Got up from where? Out of what?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: As he called the women and children away, they were physically separated from the men; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were all -- I mean, they were in two or three lines. They were standing in the field, so they were standing. They could not get up. Where could they get up from? They were standing there in the first place. So after he said that -- well, as I said, in the meantime, as he said that, one of the soldiers came there, Bosko Djuric, rather, one of the commanders, komandir, and he said that soldiers bringing weapons were arriving, and then he ordered me to go there and to take the weapons. And he continued working with these people --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. So the --

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the men and women -- or, rather -- men and women, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So the answer is that at that point you don't know the details of what went on with the group, with the women and children at the time they were being separated; is that true?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is true. I didn't see that. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Now let's go to the weapons. In paragraph 8, and I believe at your testimony earlier today, perhaps on transcript page 4, you describe that you organised the collection of weapons from the prisoners. I think it's this morning at transcript page 4 that you describe the Grabovica Company had possession of those weapons. Where did you first see the weapons?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw these weapons when I came behind the truck that was there on the road. And when soldiers started bringing that, they were bringing that individually. Some carried two pieces, others three, and so on. But they didn't arrive at the same time. Two would come and then there would be a long break and then another three men would come, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did they tell you how far they had been walking with those weapons?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. No, they didn't say how long it was that they walked. Approximately -- or, rather, it is exactly known where the position of the Grabovica Brigade was in the Duboka area. So it's from Duboka to the school, that is that distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has heard evidence that as the column surrendered, the people in the column were told that their weapons were to be placed on one side and their money and valuables on the other. Do you know what happened to the money and valuables taken from these people?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present there and I don't know of any such thing. You mean that moment when they were surrendering or, rather, as they were approaching, as they were being taken by the soldiers of the Grabovica Company?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You've said this, you weren't present for that, I accept that, for the actual surrender. But you've described that you were in charge of collecting the weapons that they left. I have told you the evidence that the Trial Chamber has heard about that process, and I'm telling you that the evidence is also that money and possessions were left in that same location. Do you know who was in charge of collecting the money and the possessions taken from the people in the column?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there at that location. I have no way of knowing. I cannot give any comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if this is a good place. If I -- I can advise you that the satellite image and a map that the Trial Chamber discussed before are now available in e-court under 65 ter 31722 and that might allow Defence counsel to take a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we all could take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have it on our screens. And could the usher already be ready to assist the witness for marking whatever appears on the screen. Could we zoom in. Could we zoom out again because we are losing the scale as well so that we all have a good idea of what the scale is. Let me just have a look. I'm just trying to -- I take it that the parties agree that approximately the horizontal -- the road which is running almost horizontally a little bit up to the north on the eastern side from where it crosses the main north-south road, that it is more than -- that the concentrated populated area is less than 2 kilometres wide. But perhaps if we have an opportunity to receive one print-out copy so that we can constantly consult the scale. Is there any way that you provide us and perhaps the parties with a --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We could. We do not have a colour printer in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's -- scale is irrespective of colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, we can do that, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then can we move -- zoom in. Could we move a little bit further to the south. Could we zoom in a little bit more, if possible. Witness, could you tell us where approximately at this moment we can find the old town and the fortress? Is it at this moment visible on our screen, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you go down a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My first question is whether it's visible or not. Is it not visible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot see that clearly there. There is something strange about this. This looks like houses there in that area, but as far as I know it -- well, it's not readily discernible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you see the location where the fortress is? Can you see it on the picture at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. At this moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it cannot be seen. It needs to be lowered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean, we need to scroll up in order to see what this is down here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we are moving now in the wrong direction. Could we move -- okay. Could you tell us when you see the fortress.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other side, the other side. The only thing we can show here is Jelsingrad, what you had asked for before. I can show it to you here now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, would you please wait for a second and follow my questioning. Do we at this moment see the fortress, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should we move more to the north, to the south, to the west, or to the east in order to see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] South.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We now move the map slightly to the north. Please tell us wherever you see the fortress.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It could be seen here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's zoom in. Do we have to move more to the south, to the north? Do we -- can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I really do not see anything here. Some houses can be seen, but no. The fortress, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It should be, as you said, I think in the old town, isn't it? Then perhaps my next question would be: Do you see the old town somewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The old town does not exist if you mean a settlement. The old town is the name of that fortress. So the old town, Stari Grad, is the name of that fortress. It's not that it's a neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see it somewhere? Perhaps we zoom out slightly so that you have a better overview. Yes. Now could you -- perhaps the -- could you have a look at what seems to be a small magnifying glass which can be moved by the usher. You see it, that one? Can you assist us in pointing at where Stari Grad is. So you just say move the pointer to the right or to the left or down or up. Give us the instructions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please speak into microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you don't speak into the microphone -- perhaps you can --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I somehow point this out to you. I mean, somehow with something with which I could indicate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you see it, try to mark it to start with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up here. Well, I went a bit down. It's up here. Roughly up here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to be somewhere in the middle of a meadow. Is that where the fortress is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a forest. There is a bit of a forest there and then there was a big meadow. As far as I can see, these houses, if they are houses, these white dots, that did not exist before. There were houses in the valley --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We can no longer hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, apart from that you cannot be heard, if you would please to start with make --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Make sure that the pointer is where the fortress is. Is it there at this moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you also tilt -- if the usher could help him tilt the microphone towards so that when he speaks and looks down -- that's better.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The fort is here where I'm marking this. That's where the position of the fortress would be. But we have here these houses, these points, these dots that are unclear to me. I don't know how come. They weren't here before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You have now more or less pointed at the -- what you consider to be the fortress. Could we zoom in on that part. Oh, it's marked. Okay. And Judge Moloto would have a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Earlier you told us that this fortress still does exist. We see dots there which you say were not there before, but I'm not seeing any dot that looks like a fortress. Could you show it to us, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's hard. I mean, there are just the foundations there and then there would be a wall about half a metre high or 20 centimetres up, and then in some places it would be 1 metre or a bit more than that. However, now it is barely discernible because, quite simply, it blended into the environment, so there aren't any elements that distinguish this in that setting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, there is a lot of vegetation growing over it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can I put an additional question. You have marked a specific location in red. Just below that, south of it, there is a half round -- yeah, something, could that be the foundation of the fortress you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. What you see down there, the semicircle, that's a road. It's a road. And there's a river there. A road and a river.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And again you confirm that where you put this marking, there is, in your view, the fortress?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I understand this image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. And you are saying that this is Stari Grad, the old town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stari Grad, the old town is the name of the fortress.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you have marked it in red? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately, approximately. I cannot do it with precision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would suggest that markings would be done again because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- the witness said, "Oh, I missed, I have to go up and" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's remove. Please try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, we should save this marking, and we can do an additional marking after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, then we'll save this one. Madam Registrar, and this would receive number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31722, page 1, as marked by the witness for the first time, receives number P6980, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's mark it for identification for the time being so that we are safe. Okay. Could we have now -- could we zoom in slightly -- well, this is nice as well but ... could we zoom in slightly on the -- a little bit further -- a little bit larger. Like that, yes. Witness, could you now with more precision mark the position of the fortress? And the usher will assist you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be it, roughly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we see a lot of constructions relatively nearby. Is it your evidence that they're all new or that they did not exist at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that close to the fortress there weren't any buildings. A bit further away, yes, as I've already mentioned, 4- or 500 metres away, some kind of houses. I don't know whether they were barns or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you indicate some of the constructions that were there already at the time? Perhaps could the usher assist. Because what we see now is that the -- the fortress is marked with a red almost full circle. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are now drawing a line. Does that mean that all the houses behind that line would have existed already but the ones closer to the fortress not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, that was the situation. Perhaps here, this point, there may have been there, but I think that these were barns or cattle sheds, rather. I don't know. It's possible that there were buildings there, but I don't remember any of the rest. The main buildings were down where the land was flat in the valley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the parties agree, one way or another, that the distance between the marking where the fortress is and where the witness drew a line, that that is approximately 200 metres? Well, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would say even more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we have it on our map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: 400 metres, in my view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have an opportunity to later check the exact distances. So what you are telling us is that the constructions above the line were there already at the time, and the constructions closer to the fortress were not there. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that they were there, whereas the buildings down there, they were there. That is about 400 or 500 metres away, in my estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. We'll later -- that's a matter of analysis and rather measuring than in any way -- Could we have this marked. Could we save this image. Unless you would have any further questions, Ms. Bibles, so that we could do the marking right away?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes. I do just have one question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In this same order, there is a portion which talks about fire on the forest Lipik, L-i-p-i-k, is that close to this particular location?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember anymore where Lipik is. I don't know exactly where it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have saved this. Could we zoom out. And could you now tell us where the firing position was, as you said, I think it was a factory. Could you mark that with the assistance of the usher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Jelsingrad, I think it was. Could you tell us where that is? You have marked that one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I marked that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a factory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Matters are now perfectly clear to me. There is one matter to be resolved. That is, I'm still puzzled by an area far away from what seems to be the centre of Kotor Varos town, to be called Stari Grad; whereas, in many other villages and cities Stari Grad is in the very centre of a city. So that still puzzles me somewhat. So if there is any other evidence which would further support the understanding that Stari Grad is not where it is everywhere else but is instead relatively far away from the centre of town --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- if you go now on internet and you punch "Stari Grad Kotor Varos" you'll get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- I'm only too happy to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just tried now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I must admit that the Judges have access to internet, and we could give it a -- we could give it a try and see --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- well, the question would be how we would capture the evidence that the Trial Chamber is considering. It's obviously an internet address so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that. What I could do -- let's be very --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we first save this marked image so that we will not lose it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we perhaps could do best, Mr. Lukic, if you give us an address which makes it visible, then we would have that on the record. And then we could later make a electronic version of that. So if you could give us the -- is it on Google maps or is it somewhere --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just Kotor Varos. Okay. Then I'll read what -- let's have a look. If you would -- Ms. Bibles --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- anyhow, otherwise I would have invited you to continue. What we'll do, Mr. Lukic, we'll follow your suggestion, and we'll all during the break exclusively look for "Stari Grad Kotor Varos" and then when coming back in court we might if you have already --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Ivetic can, with the assistance of the Registrar, Ms. Registrar, put it on our screens, if you want.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: A screen print would be preferable to searching off the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I would also note that 65 ter 31722, which has been uploaded, is not just the aerial but is also a topographical map which has features, and I would just bring that to everyone's attention just before we break to take a look at these items.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think I see where we are. It's -- okay. We save this for after the break, but we could have a look at it already. It seems, indeed, that there is an elevation in that area, if I look at the elevation lines, and we'll -- Mr. Ivetic will then assist us after the break so that the Chamber will not search itself. I think that's a better --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on our screens now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- position. It's on your screens. Let's have a look at it after the break. Let's -- we'll -- Witness, we'll take a break of 20 minutes and we'd like to see you back after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Ms. Bibles, this whole exercise started with questioning the witness about a military order in which the -- an artillery preparation for an attack was ordered, including concentrated fire on, as it was said, the old town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness now says that the old town is not what usually is the old town but that it's an mainly non-inhabited area somewhere south-west of the centre of Kotor Varos town. Is there further dispute about that? I take it that you have taken your time during the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- in terms of the instant discussion that we've had with respect to old town, the Court's correct. I would simply note that the order spanned other locations for concentrated fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Other locations are still to be seen. I leave it to you whether you want to further explore that. But is there any remaining dispute about Stari Grad translated as "old town" not being the centre of the town of Kotor Varos but, rather, on a hilly area which is at quite a distance from the centre of town and in an area which, at least on maps, seems to be not densely populated in any way?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would agree that -- and I had not intended to infer that "old town" was the centre of Kotor Varos. And I would absolutely agree with that, that it is in the locations that we've identified on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There was at least the suggestion of attacking populated areas, whereas the name might mislead us. And I think that, under those circumstances, but I'm also looking at you, Mr. Lukic, there is no further reason to explore that. Apart from any other geographic location perhaps mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I would agree with that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then let's move on. I leave it to the parties whether they still want to tender a picture or whatever, but I don't think that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After this, there is no need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 31722 which included the topographical map. Since we did have a discussion, I think it would be appropriate to tender both the aerial and the topographical map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There is no objections --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I take it. Madam Registrar. Well, let's try to keep it simple. We'll later discuss what is then admitted into evidence or what is not. I have to verify that again. But at this moment we are talking about the geographical map, 31722. Madam Registrar, it would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31722 receives number P6981, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, I am finishing here, and I have a couple of questions that I will try to focus very tightly. I would like to go back to Grabovica and the list of the men that you've described creating. First, did you recognise or know any of the men that you saw that night?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't recognise them. But I can give an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No. I just want brief answers, thank you. Would you agree that the men were all either Muslim or Croat?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that the list that you compiled was of the individuals that were brought by twos or threes into the office -- or into the classroom I believe your testimony actually was? You would agree that it is possible that there are individuals who were captured in that group or who were in the group who were in the upper floor of the school that, for whatever reason, were not brought to you?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what I --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I could comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, give this list to Colonel Novakovic the next morning?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Have you ever seen the list since? Have you seen the list since that date?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In paragraph 16, you explain being ordered to return to the brigade command post in Kotor Varos. In paragraph 20, you describe telling the commander of the company about what happened. Who was this commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment. [In English] It might create confusion. Maybe my learned friend misspoke. And it is said "company commander," so I don't think it's in paragraph 20 that it was mentioned "company commander."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Line 1 it's "command of the company."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Command of the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Command of the" -- and "informed whom," it says "command then." In B/C/S, it's higher rank than company commander. Maybe it should be clarified first who he informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And that was all I was asking.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is: Who did you inform in paragraph 20?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed the commander of the brigade, Dusan Novakovic, who was at the Grabovica Company command at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That clarifies matters. All right. In paragraph 21, you say -- actually, I'll first ask: You've describe that you went to the Grabovica command. Where was that actually located in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The company command actually was located in three buildings: The school, the old school, and three residential buildings. And the company command was actually located in the old school.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. And the -- and just to clarify, I believe it's evident in your statement but just to make it clear, the people from the column were put in a new school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Now in paragraph 21, you tell us that you had the impression that you were intentionally moved away from, I believe it's Kotor Varos, by Lieutenant-Colonel Novakovic in the days after you left Grabovica. Can you describe for us just briefly how many days or how long did this time-period last?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It lasted for three days, perhaps. Three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, if we could have P852 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: This is a 4 November 1992 extract of the War Presidency. And it's one page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the War Presidency of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I will be asking you to look at item 2. And actually I forgot to ask you a question before about the list. How many men were on your list?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember how many men were on the list. I gave the number of women based on logical reasoning, because they were located in this classroom where I actually drafted the list. I didn't see a group of men at any point in time that was separate in order to be able to estimate the number, and that is what I said in my statement, the one that I gave to Mr. Mirko Kosic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Was it over 50 men?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my estimation, based on what you could see when Commander Novakovic was trying to bring some light where that group was, I think that, based on what I could see, there were about 150 men there. But this is just an estimate.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not definite.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm not seeing P852. I don't know if my screen is -- ah, there we go. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, this is the 4 November 1992 extract from the War Presidency. I would like to take you to item number 2, Captain Slobodan Zupljanin reports that 150 soldiers and civilians surrendered. The next paragraph states that Pejic, Zupljanin, Balaban, and Novakovic "shall decide on the fate of the soldiers who were taken prisoner." Now, is it true that Novakovic was the commander in charge when you left Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the very virtue of his post, he was in charge of those people while they were in Grabovica. As for anything relating to this document, I don't have any knowledge of that. The only thing I can say, if you permit me --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you've answered my question. Sir, you've told us that you were not there when these men were killed, so you can't tell us who killed the men. But can you confirm that these captured men were, in fact, the responsibility of the Kotor Varos Light Brigade of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Bibles. Mr. Lukic, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was a bit of a surprise. I am not organised. Give me half a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll give you half a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krsic, good day once again.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The topic of Grabovica, is that something that was openly discussed in Kotor Varos? Was it easy to have access to any information?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we are talking about Grabovica, Grabovica simply became taboo. It was not a topic that was discussed, and it's not discussed to this day. Nobody wants to talk about the problem of Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at P4296, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were shown this document. Item 5 of the document, which is a document of the 1st Krajina Corps command, states that the 122nd -- it states that the Skender Vakuf and Kotor Varos Light Brigades are resubordinated to the 122nd Light Infantry Brigade. What does this information indicate? Is it customary for an entire brigade to be resubordinated to another brigade?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally this was not applied in practice. Parts of certain units could be resubordinated, but a unit as a whole, that was not the practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what led to this, i.e., that your entire brigade would be resubordinated to the 122nd, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This indicates that the responsibility for that area was given to the 122nd Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you know how long was your -- your brigade resubordinated to the 122nd Light Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly. This is just proof of the fact that, as the Kotor Varos Brigade, we did not have direct communications with the corps command and did not receive orders directly from them. Communications between the 1st Krajina Corps and the Kotor Varos Brigade only began in late October.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the dates? I think it was not correctly noted in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it was from November onwards when the communications intensified between the two commands, the Kotor Varos Brigade and the 1st Krajina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at P6979 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We already see in this "order to attack." You were shown item 5.11.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which is on the fourth page in the English and on the third page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to look at that same item with you, please. We see here, after having clarified what the old town was, and we're talking about concentrated fire on the old town, a barrage of fire on the slope east of the Gubavac stream. We have received interpretation now, but could you please explain what "barrage fire" is?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the military terminology when we're talking about artillery fire, there is concentrated fire and barrage fire. Concentrated fire means firing from several weapons into one target, whereas barrage means that fire is opened from each of the weapons at a certain distance between the explosions of the shells that are being fired at a certain area. The objective of barrage fire is to prevent infantry forces of the enemy from coming closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I think that we have an issue with the translation at this point of time, Your Honours. At 5.11, under a, when it says "barrage of fire." So I think that it has some kind of different meaning than what "zaprecna vatra" clearly means in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If there is any translation issue, we'll deal with that quietly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if there is any question related to that, perhaps you can put it to the witness without using the contested words or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that he explained --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- so I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When there is mention of concentrated fire on K334 --

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you explain the village of Duratovci and the village of Ravne. At the time do you know if enemy forces were deployed on the outer edge of those villages?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Muslim-Croat forces were deployed on the edge of that area. And if I may just add something about what we see here. Perhaps there was an error made here when they mention directly the village of Ravne. What should be said here is the sector of Ravne. That would be more specific, more precise, and then there wouldn't be so many problems in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that that it is misinterpreted, or do you say that is what they should have written in that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They should have written that in the order. It's not a translation error, but actually that was omitted from the actual order and it should have been there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's an opinion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Now, let's look at the first page of both versions of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you this. You already started to explain. I'm interested in item 2, but there is no need for you to focus on that so much right now. Does something else accompany a written order; maps, are they drawn?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Each order consists of a written order as well as a topographic map and a graphical representation of the area indicating the disposition of the units, the main axis of attack, and the auxiliary axis of attack. Also, the map would show the planned fire, the planned artillery fire, and that is used in order to prepare elements for fire in certain sections. Whether the fire would actually be executed or not would depend on the conditions in the actual theater.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If fire was opened in this action on civilian targets, do you think there would have been any civilian casualties and can you perhaps tell how many?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there should have been civilian casualties, quite substantial ones. It was a densely populated area and the women and children would particularly have been among the casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After those days, did you come to learn that many civilians had lost their lives in that operation?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just in relation to this list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I have one question. One of the previous answers which puzzles me, page 90, line 11, you said, well, if civilian targets would have been engaged, then there should have been civilian casualties, quite substantial ones. And then you said: "It was a densely populated area." Which area were you exactly referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The village of Ravne, up there, which is south-west of the centre of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That village is mentioned in point 2, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I know that it was. And you say that it's to the south-west of Kotor Varos town? Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm closing to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You spoke to me and to my colleague about the list, the list of men that you made, and she asked you whether you were sure that there might have been someone who you had not listed. Did you give instructions to the people, the soldiers of the Army of Republika Srpska, who were guarding these people? Did you tell them to bring them all when these lists were being made?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The soldiers were told when they had this role of escorting people from one courtroom -- from one --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Classroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to the other, that they should all be brought for this list to be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more topic, two questions or so. You said that you saw roughly about 150 persons when Novakovic was turning on the lights on the people who were being brought in. These 150 persons, did he include only women -- only men, or were women included in these 150? Who was included?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly we included the people who were brought in, so women, children, and men in my estimate. Around there, there were some people from my unit, too. So it was hard to assess what the actual number was. That is why I really cannot be certain about this number. So it was a group of people there. In addition to them, there were the members of our own army there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsic, thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV KRSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, any further questions? But let me first check whether my colleagues have any questions. Any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the Bench also has no questions, Mr. Krsic, I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered the many questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One final matter. P6980 was MFI'd. That was the aerial view with a rather -- well, a bit of a clumsy marking on it. Then we had -- we have saved two follow-up marked aerial photographs, the one that was saved indicated where Stari Grad was with a line where the witness said where houses already in existence north of that. And then the last photograph that was marked was the facility, the industrial facility, from where the fire would -- was ordered to be prepared for. I suggest that we get them all under this one number, 6980. Therefore, Madam Registrar, could you please attach to what is now P6980 MFI'd, could you attach to that the two follow-up saved marked aerial photographs, and then all three together are admitted as P6980. Then we adjourn for the day and we resume Monday, the 8th of December, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
